title: Tiered price experiment + hiring triggers (sprint heatmap)
summary: Working spreadsheet that maps a series of tiered pricing experiments (per-region, per-tier) to explicit hiring triggers and a sprint-based heatmap. Purpose: give GTM + Eng a short, operational runbook for when to convert temporary contractors to full-time hires or request burst capacity based on realized elasticity and revenue delta during controlled price tests.
assumptions: Base ARR: $28.4M; current headcount in Cost of Goods Sold (infra + ops) = 42 FTEs; baseline price tiers: Free, Starter, Growth, Enterprise. Experiment window: 8 sprints (16 weeks). Elasticity bands estimated from pilot data: low (0–0.3 revenue delta), medium (0.3–1.2), high (>1.2). Cost per new infra hire (ramp-ready) = $210k fully-loaded/year; contractor equivalent = $65k for 4 months. Forecast conversion lag = 2 sprints.

scenario_definitions:
A_low_risk: cap price lift to +5% across non-enterprise tiers; use contractors only; revenue delta expected 0–0.5%.
B_mid_risk: tiered lifts (Starter +12%, Growth +8%) in two regions simultaneously; pre-approve conversion of 50% contractor pool if regional delta > +1% sustained for 2 sprints.
C_high_risk_high-reward: aggressive lift (Starter +18–25%) with expanded geographical coverage and fast-track hiring: immediate FT offer for infra roles if observed +2% revenue delta; requires SLA with Talent/People ops.
financial_sensitivities:
Quick sensitivity snapshots (petty-format):
- If starter-tier price elasticity < 0.5: revenue upside minimal; avoid FT commitments.
- If elasticity between 0.5–1.5: contractor-to-FT conversion yields payback in 9–12 months.
- If elasticity > 1.5 in a region for Starter tier: prioritize dedicated capacity (Dedicated pool) and accelerate hiring ladder; predicted uplift covers 1.5x incremental infra run-rate within 6 months.
Note: all scenarios include a safety cap: stop-loss of -3% net ARR vs control for any region -> immediate rollback.
unit_economics_snapshot: Per-customer LTV uplift by tier (approx): Starter: +$620 LTV with +12% price; Growth: +$1,900 with +8% price; Enterprise: +$12k with +6% price. Incremental infra cost per 10k additional token-units/month: ~$14k (GPU-hours + networking). Payback horizon sensitivity table maintained in linked confluence page.
recommended_actions:
1) Approve sprint heatmap and tagging in experiment board (JIRA-FIN-3421).
2) Pre-allocate contractor pool budget (Q4 flex) to cover mid-risk path.
3) Authorize People Ops to fast-track 2 infra hires if any single region Starter-tier shows > +2% sustained revenue delta for two sprints.
4) Ensure Dedicated capacity procurement options are priced and queued prior to S4 in EU (Procurement ticket PR-647).
5) Run daily revenue deltas and publish via Slack #pricing-experiments digest for Finance/Eng/PM leads.
open_questions_and_notes:
- Data fidelity: need per-region token mix adjustments; current analytics assumes uniform usage distribution which is false for Enterprise customers.
- Experiment overlap risk: multiple simultaneous tier tests may confound elasticity; prefer staggered start per region where possible.
- Legal review: ensure price changes comply with regional tax/regulation (VAT notifications).
- Tracking: add unique experiment identifier to invoice metadata to attribute bookings.
- Notes-to-self: follow up with Hiring Ops on contractor conversion SLA and with Infra Eng on burst-capacity SLAs.
conclusion: This sheet translates pricing sensitivity signals into operational hiring triggers on a sprint cadence. It is intentionally conservative on FT commitments unless we observe high elasticity (>1.5) sustained across two sprints. Primary recommendation: run B_mid_risk in US + EU first, with pre-approved contractor conversion and a fast-track FT threshold for infra when metrics clear. Review results at end of S4 and decide on Q3 headcount commitments.
